acceptance_requirements: Retain the full frozen milestone_01_r02_player_locomotion_contract; this bounded increment does not redefine or independently pass R02.
Default B owns roll; E and F retain interaction and old-lamp ownership. Unavailable equipment remains gated.
Adjustable bindings, effective controls and displayed prompts agree on the selected locomotion surface.
deferred_items: Host-deferred cinematic, camera obstruction, grass dependency, connected-slice evidence and demo presentation findings remain mandatory backlog without current-loop tasks.
Later milestone gaps and unimplemented interaction, lamp, combat and narrative systems remain outside this bounded increment.
implied_completion: A binding change must affect ordinary player input and visible prompts; editing a declaration alone is insufficient.
Binding capture must consume its input without triggering traversal, shoulder switching or attacks, and returning control must require fresh action input.
A locked old lamp must not cause F to fall back to roll.
mandatory_objectives: Treat r02-input-bindings within one coherent locomotion-control increment.
Restore default B/F ownership and provide player-accessible rebinding for the active R02 controls.
Preserve verified shoulder, locomotion, animation, equipment-gating and mouse-look behavior.
Leave issue and phase closure to current candidate-bound Host and Tester evidence.
task_specification.objective: Deliver adjustable locomotion controls whose effective bindings and prompts agree, beginning with default B roll and reserved F ownership, while preserving the existing unarmed village traversal slice.

diagnosis.root_cause: The adopted controller still dispatches roll directly from KEY_F, has no KEY_B dispatch, polls locomotion keys directly, and maintains a separate hard-coded help string. Prior live observations confirm B does nothing while F rolls and the InputMap contains only built-in UI actions. The previous Tab/E repair corrected one assignment but left adjustable input ownership and prompt synchronization unfinished.

stop_conditions: Stop scope expansion after this single control-binding increment; do not absorb deferred presentation, asset or narrative work.
If the selected actor or traversal dependency is genuinely missing, report the exact dependency and preserve the frozen resource selection.
If registered ordinary-input capture or authoritative state observation is unavailable, report insufficient evidence and the Host dependency; do not invent receipts or weaken acceptance.
Do not declare the issue closed from source inspection, candidate-authored success flags or Developer self-validation.
Any regression in the preserved native boot, shoulder, equipment or locomotion behavior prevents completion.

strategy.rationale: Change strategy from isolated key substitutions to repairing the relationship between configurable controls, input consumers and prompts. Direct restoration of the demo would restore its incompatible F assignment; another B-only patch would leave configurability unfinished. Replacing the qualified actor/controller resources is unnecessary because Roll playback and recovery already worked through F. Adapt input ownership around the existing traversal behavior, retain the current resources, and isolate unavailable interaction/lamp actions behind their existing ownership requirements.

code: Review all changed input consumers and prompt sources for agreement with effective bindings, including event handlers and held-input polling.
Confirm no default F-to-roll or E-to-shoulder path remains and binding-capture inputs cannot also reach gameplay consumers.
Run required native project and boot preservation checks; inspect affected logs for new input, resource or animation errors.
runtime: Host and Tester replay the original grounded unarmed B/F scenario through registered ordinary inputs. Observe action before, during and after B, advancing Roll playback, displacement and recovery; repeat F separately.

Operate the controls surface through external input: capture Roll B-to-U, inspect the effective binding, close controls, test U and B, then restore defaults and retest B. Candidate self-reports supplement rather than replace the observed journey.
Check control-capture cancellation and return: capture keys do not move, roll, switch shoulders or attack; no held action resumes until fresh input.

Preserve Tab twice with stable world facing and smooth shoulder interpolation, E without shoulder switching, walking/sprinting, jump/landing, Alt dodge recovery, unarmed equipment gates and mouse-look release/recovery. Exercise every changed held-input consumer with its effective binding.
visual: Capture the ordinary view before Roll, during visible Roll and after recovery, with enough actor visibility to judge facing and animation.
Capture default, rebound and restored control prompts plus binding-capture feedback; compare displayed keys with the actual external-input outcomes.
Use the supplied gameplay references only for relevant camera and control readability. Full HUD/menu art replacement remains deferred.

done_when: During grounded unarmed exploration with default bindings, one B press starts Roll with advancing playback and movement consistent with the visible facing or movement direction, then returns to controllable idle or walking; F never starts Roll.
Using ordinary in-game controls, the player rebinds Roll from B to an unused U key: the prompt updates, U starts Roll and B no longer does; restoring defaults restores the B prompt and behavior.
tasks.instructions: Bind this repair to PRD 3.2 and ISSUE-0003 on the frozen loop-03 candidate. Reproduce B/F ownership before editing. Repair configurable control ownership across the currently active R02 locomotion and shoulder controls, including their event-driven and held-input consumers and visible help. Keep implementation choice open; an engine mapping declaration is insufficient when consumers bypass it. Provide a player-accessible change and restore path on the current controls surface, with readable effective key prompts and clear capture/cancel feedback. Use Roll B-to-U-to-default as the bounded observable rebind sequence. Preserve default WASD, Space, Shift, Alt and Tab behavior; keep E/F reserved and retain equipment unlock gates. Prevent the key used during binding capture from also operating the world, and prevent held actions from leaking when controls return. Preserve existing Roll entry, clip progression, direction, cooldown and recovery rather than retuning animation or transforms without evidence. Retain the complete Ranger and authored village bindings. Any additional observation must expose actual binding or traversal state, never a duplicate QA state machine or pass flag. Developer performs focused self-validation; Host and Tester own independent recapture, formal review and closure. Report any unimplemented or unmeasured portion of the issue's full acceptance explicitly.

investigation.expected_observation: The baseline trace shows F reaching evade("roll") independently of configurable action bindings and the help text independently naming F. A declared binding change alone cannot affect a bypassing consumer. After repair, ordinary rebinding changes dispatch and prompts together while the existing traversal state machine remains unchanged.
investigation.hypothesis: The repeated failure comes from demo key ownership being distributed between raw-key dispatch, held-key polling and static prompts, rather than a Roll animation defect.
investigation.probe: Trace the existing configuration source, key consumers and prompt source for Roll and the active locomotion controls. Pair that trace with the original ordinary B/F input sequence. Compare direct demo restoration, isolated key substitution and adaptation of binding ownership before editing. After the chosen repair, use the public controls path to perform B-to-U-to-default and repeat the same input
